units.t: Native American Traditions and Colonial Voices

learn: Before European contact, Native nations kept histories, laws and stories through oral tradition.
The Iroquois Confederacy's Great Law of Peace united five (later six) nations.
Origin stories, such as the Haudenosaunee Sky Woman story, explain the world and values.
check: The Great Law of Peace united the...
lessons.try: Compare two Native origin stories and the values they express.

learn: Puritans saw life as a test of faith; plain style was valued.
William Bradford's "Of Plymouth Plantation" records the colony's hardships.
Anne Bradstreet's poems mix devotion with personal feeling.
lessons.try: Analyse how Bradstreet's "Upon the Burning of Our House" balances loss and faith.

learn: Jonathan Edwards's "Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God" (1741) used vivid imagery to persuade.
Mary Rowlandson's narrative (1682) describes her captivity during King Philip's War.
Reading these texts critically means noticing whose perspective is missing.
check: Edwards's sermon was part of the...
lessons.try: Identify three persuasive images in Edwards's sermon.

learn: Ethos appeals to credibility, pathos to emotion, logos to logic.
Kairos means the right moment for an argument.
Revolutionary writers combined all four.
lessons.try: Label ethos, pathos and logos in a short speech.

learn: Thomas Paine's "Common Sense" (1776) argued in plain language for independence.
"The Crisis" opens: "These are the times that try men's souls."
Patrick Henry's 1775 speech ends "Give me liberty, or give me death!"
check: "Give me liberty, or give me death!" is from...
lessons.try: Explain why Paine chose plain language for a mass audience.

learn: Jefferson's Declaration has a preamble, a statement of rights, grievances and a conclusion.
Its claim that "all men are created equal" was later used by abolitionists and suffragists.
Abigail Adams urged her husband to "remember the ladies".
check: "All men are created equal" was later used by...
lessons.try: Map the structure of the Declaration's argument.

learn: American Romanticism (1820-1865) celebrated emotion, imagination, nature and the individual.
Writers drew on American landscapes and folklore.
Washington Irving's "Rip Van Winkle" set legends in the Hudson Valley.
lessons.try: List Romantic traits in "Rip Van Winkle".

learn: Dark Romantics explored guilt, sin, madness and the supernatural.
Poe's "The Tell-Tale Heart" and "The Fall of the House of Usher" build a single effect.
Hawthorne's "The Scarlet Letter" (1850) examines guilt and judgment in Puritan Boston.
lessons.try: Analyse how Poe uses an unreliable narrator.

learn: Melville's "Moby-Dick" (1851) uses Ahab's hunt for the whale to explore obsession.
Emily Dickinson wrote nearly 1,800 short poems with dashes and slant rhyme.
"Because I could not stop for Death" personifies death as a carriage driver.
check: In "Because I could not stop for Death", death is a...
lessons.try: Analyse slant rhyme in a Dickinson poem.

learn: Transcendentalists believed truth is found through intuition and nature.
Emerson's "Self-Reliance" (1841) urges trust in yourself: "Trust thyself."
"Nature" (1836) describes becoming a "transparent eyeball".
lessons.try: Write a response agreeing or disagreeing with a line from "Self-Reliance".

learn: "Walden" (1854) records two years living simply by Walden Pond.
"Civil Disobedience" (1849) argues people should refuse to support unjust laws.
It influenced Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr.
lessons.try: Simplify one routine in your life for a week and reflect.

learn: Walt Whitman's "Leaves of Grass" (1855) pioneered American free verse.
"Song of Myself" celebrates the self and all people equally.
His long lines and catalogues create a democratic voice.
check: "Leaves of Grass" was first published in...
lessons.try: Write a short catalogue poem in Whitman's style.

units.t: Voices of Slavery, Freedom and the Civil War

learn: Douglass's "Narrative" (1845) describes his enslavement, learning to read and escape.
He saw literacy as "the pathway from slavery to freedom".
"What to the Slave Is the Fourth of July?" (1852) exposes American hypocrisy.
check: Douglass saw literacy as a path to...
The Fourth of July speech exposes...
lessons.try: Analyse Douglass's rhetorical appeals in the Fourth of July speech.

learn: Harriet Jacobs's "Incidents in the Life of a Slave Girl" (1861) describes the abuses faced by enslaved women.
Sojourner Truth's "Ain't I a Woman?" linked abolition and women's rights.
Spirituals carried coded hopes for freedom.
lessons.try: Compare Jacobs's and Douglass's purposes and audiences.

learn: The Gettysburg Address (1863) redefined the war as a fight for equality in 272 words.
The Second Inaugural (1865) called for "malice toward none, with charity for all".
Lincoln used parallelism and biblical cadence.
check: The Gettysburg Address is about ___ words.
lessons.try: Identify parallel structures in the Gettysburg Address.

learn: Realism (1865-1900) portrayed ordinary life truthfully, without idealisation.
Writers focused on middle- and working-class characters.
Henry James and William Dean Howells were leading Realists.
lessons.try: Compare a Romantic and a Realist passage.

learn: "Adventures of Huckleberry Finn" (1884) uses dialect and satire to criticise racism.
Huck's choice to help Jim escape is the novel's moral centre.
Readers today discuss its racial language and its anti-racist aims.
lessons.try: Analyse a passage where Huck wrestles with his conscience.

learn: Regionalists captured local dialect and customs (Kate Chopin in Louisiana, Sarah Orne Jewett in Maine).
Naturalists (Stephen Crane, Jack London) showed people shaped by forces beyond their control.
Chopin's "The Story of an Hour" (1894) explores a woman's sudden sense of freedom.
lessons.try: Discuss the ending of "The Story of an Hour".

learn: Modernism (1914-1945) responded to war and rapid change with experiment and fragmentation.
T.S. Eliot's "The Waste Land" (1922) and Ezra Pound's Imagism broke traditions.
Robert Frost used traditional forms with modern doubts: "The Road Not Taken" (1916).
lessons.try: Discuss common misreadings of "The Road Not Taken".

learn: In the 1920s Harlem became a centre of Black art, music and literature.
Langston Hughes's "The Negro Speaks of Rivers" (1921) links Black history to great rivers.
Zora Neale Hurston and Claude McKay were key writers.
check: "The Negro Speaks of Rivers" is by...
The Harlem Renaissance took place in the...
lessons.try: Analyse jazz rhythms in a Hughes poem.

learn: F. Scott Fitzgerald's "The Great Gatsby" (1925) critiques the American Dream in the Jazz Age.
Nick Carraway narrates Gatsby's longing for Daisy.
The green light symbolises unreachable hopes.
check: "The Great Gatsby" is set in the...
lessons.try: Trace the green light through the novel.

learn: Arthur Miller's "Death of a Salesman" (1949) shows Willy Loman broken by false dreams of success.
"The Crucible" (1953) uses the Salem witch trials to comment on McCarthyism.
Lorraine Hansberry's "A Raisin in the Sun" (1959) follows a Black family's hopes in Chicago.
check: "A Raisin in the Sun" is set in...
lessons.try: Compare the dreams of Willy Loman and the Younger family.

learn: William Faulkner used stream of consciousness and invented Yoknapatawpha County.
Flannery O'Connor's stories use violence and grace.
Southern Gothic mixes the grotesque with moral questions.
check: Southern Gothic mixes the grotesque with...
lessons.try: Identify Southern Gothic elements in a short story.

learn: Ralph Ellison's "Invisible Man" (1952) explores Black identity and invisibility.
The Beat writers rebelled against conformity.
Novels examined alienation and civil rights.
lessons.try: Discuss the meaning of "invisible" in Ellison's prologue.

learn: Contemporary literature includes Toni Morrison, Sandra Cisneros, Amy Tan and Sherman Alexie.
Writers explore identity, family, immigration and memory.
Morrison won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993.
check: Morrison won the Nobel Prize in...
"The House on Mango Street" is by...
lessons.try: Read a vignette from "The House on Mango Street" and write your own.

learn: Poets like Rita Dove, Joy Harjo and Ocean Vuong use varied forms.
Joy Harjo was the first Native American US Poet Laureate (2019).
Spoken word brings poetry to performance.
check: Joy Harjo was the first Native American...
lessons.try: Write and perform a spoken-word piece.

learn: Memoirs (James Baldwin's essays, Ta-Nehisi Coates) blend personal and political.
Creative nonfiction uses literary techniques for true stories.
Evaluate how authors build credibility.
lessons.try: Write a personal essay linking your experience to a larger issue.

learn: A synthesis essay combines multiple sources to support your own argument.
Your claim leads; sources support it, not replace it.
Show how sources agree, disagree or add nuance.
lessons.try: Read four sources on a topic and write a thesis that uses three.

learn: Analyse how an author achieves a purpose, not whether you agree.
Discuss choices: diction, structure, appeals, evidence.
Use precise verbs: emphasises, contrasts, illustrates.
lessons.try: Write a rhetorical analysis of a famous speech.

learn: Evaluate sources for authority, accuracy, currency and bias.
Integrate quotations smoothly and cite in MLA.
Avoid plagiarism; paraphrase accurately and credit ideas.
lessons.try: Write a 1,500-word researched argument with a Works Cited page.
